questions.stem:
At time $t$ seconds ($0 \leqslant t < 5$), a particle $P$ has velocity $\mathbf{v}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, where
$\mathbf{v} = \left(\sqrt{5-t}\right)\mathbf{i} + \left(t^2+2t-3\right)\mathbf{j}$
When $t=\lambda$, particle $P$ is moving in a direction parallel to the vector $\mathbf{i}$.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\lambda^2+2\lambda-3=0 \, (=(\lambda+3)(\lambda-1))$ M1: Set j component = 0 and solve for $\lambda$
$\Rightarrow \lambda=1$ A1: Only. Seen or implied. Accept t=1
Use $a=\frac{d\mathbf{v}}{dt}$ M1: Attempt derivative of both components with respect to t. Powers going down. Condone errors in dealing with the signs/indices for the square root. The answer must be a vector.
$=\frac{-1}{2\sqrt{5-t}}\mathbf{i}+(2t+2)\mathbf{j}$ A1: Any equivalent form
$=-\frac{1}{4}\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}$ A1: Only. Any equivalent form. ISW if they go on to find the magnitude.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The position vector of $P$ is measured relative to the fixed point $O$
When $t=1$, the position vector of $P$ is $(-2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m}$.

Given that $1 \leqslant T < 5$

(b) find, in terms of $T$, the position vector of $P$ when $t=T$
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) Use $s=\int v\,dt$ M1: Attempt integral of both components. (M0 if they have assumed that one component is zero) Powers going up. Condone errors in dealing with the signs/indices for the square root.
$s=\left(-\frac{2}{3}(5-t)^{3/2}(+A)\right)\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{1}{3}t^3+t^2-3t(+B)\right)\mathbf{j}$ A1 A1: Unsimplified expression with error in at most one term. Correct unsimplified expression. Allow with no constant(s) of integration.
Use $t=1$, $s=-2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$ DM1: Use of initial condition to find constant(s) of integration. Dependent on the previous M1.
$s=\left(-\frac{2}{3}(5-T)^{3/2}+\frac{10}{3}\right)\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{1}{3}T^3+T^2-3T+\frac{8}{3}\right)\mathbf{j}$ A1: Any equivalent form for the position vector.

questions.stem:
Figure 1 shows a uniform rod $AB$ of length $8a$ and weight $W$.
The end $A$ of the rod is freely hinged to horizontal ground.
The rod rests in equilibrium against a block which is also fixed to the ground.
The block is modelled as a smooth solid hemisphere with radius $2a$ and centre $D$.
The point of contact between the rod and the block is $C$, where $AC=5a$
The rod is at an angle $\theta$ to the ground, as shown in Figure 1.
Points $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ all lie in the same vertical plane.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme: (a) $AD=\sqrt{(2a)^2+(5a)^2}=\sqrt{29}a$ B1*: Correct use of Pythagoras to show given answer from correct working (need a on both sides)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Show that the magnitude of the normal reaction at $C$ between the rod and the block is $\frac{4}{\sqrt{29}}W$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M(A): $W\times 4a\cos\theta = N\times 5a$ M1: Dimensionally correct equation in a. Allow if a cancelled. Condone sin/cos confusion
$W\times 4a\times\frac{5}{\sqrt{29}}=N\times 5a$ A1: Correct unsimplified equation. Allow with $\cos\theta$. NB: $5a=\sqrt{29}a\cos\theta$
$N=\frac{4}{\sqrt{29}}W$ A1*: Obtain given answer from correct working

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The resultant force acting on the rod at $A$ has magnitude $kW$ and acts at an angle $\alpha$ to the ground.

(c) Find (i) the exact value of $k$
(ii) the exact value of $\tan\alpha$
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) The candidates need to form sufficient equations to solve for k and $\tan\alpha$. There should be two independent equations. Allow M1A1 for the first equation seen, and M1A1 for the second equation. If there are more than 2 equations, award the marks for the equations used to solve for k and $\tan\alpha$. If they stop after forming the equations, allow the marks for the best 2 equations.
Resolve vertically M1: Requires all relevant terms. Condone sin/cos confusion
$V+N\cos\theta=W$ $\left(V=\frac{9}{29}W\right)$ A1: Correct unsimplified equation. Need not substitute for trig.
Resolve horizontally M1: Requires all relevant terms. Condone consistent sin/cos confusion
$H=N\sin\theta \left(=\frac{8}{29}W\right)$ A1: Correct unsimplified equation. Need not substitute for trig.
Possible alternative equation for M1A1 using M(C): $aW\cos\theta+5aH\sin\theta=5aV\cos\theta$ or $aW\cos\theta=kW\times 5a\sin(\alpha-\theta)$
Use Pythagoras to obtain k: $k^2=\left(\frac{9}{29}\right)^2+\left(\frac{8}{29}\right)^2$ DM1: Correct use of perpendicular components. Dependent on the first 2 M marks
$k=\frac{\sqrt{145}}{29}=\sqrt{\frac{5}{29}}$ A1: Correct only. Any equivalent exact form (ISW but 0.415 with no exact answer seen is A0)
Use trig to obtain $\tan\alpha$ DM1: Dependent on the first 2 M marks
$\tan\alpha=\frac{9}{8}$ A1: Correct only. Must be a simplified number. Do not accept answer including W

Alternative method:
Resolve parallel to rod M1: Requires all relevant terms. Condone sin/cos confusion
$F=W\sin\theta \left(=\frac{2}{\sqrt{29}}W\right)$ A1: Correct unsimplified equation. Need not substitute for trig.
Resolve perpendicular to rod M1: Requires all relevant terms. Condone consistent sin/cos confusion
$E+N=W\cos\theta$ $\left(E=\frac{1}{\sqrt{29}}W\right)$ A1: Correct unsimplified equation. Need not substitute for trig.
Possible alternative equation for M1A1 using M(C): $aW\cos\theta+5aH\sin\theta=5aV\cos\theta$ or $aW\cos\theta=kW\times 5a\sin(\alpha-\theta)$
Use Pythagoras to obtain k M1: Correct use of Pythagoras
$k=\frac{1}{\sqrt{29}}\sqrt{1+4}=\sqrt{\frac{5}{29}}$ A1: Correct only
Use trig to obtain $\tan\alpha$: $\tan(\alpha-\theta)=\frac{1}{2}=\frac{\tan\alpha-\frac{2}{5}}{1+\frac{2}{5}\tan\alpha}$ DM1: Use of trig to obtain expression in $\tan\alpha$
$\tan\alpha=\frac{9}{8}$ A1: Correct only
Official notes (completeness pass):
- or $kW\sin\alpha+N\cos\theta=W$
- or $kW\cos\alpha=N\sin\theta\left(=\frac{8}{29}W\right)$
